meta.title: Generic stablecoin ecosystem research
meta.scope: Public primary market context plus explicitly synthetic demo examples. No recurring collection.
meta.coverage: Ten primary sources and ten named organizations. Market facts concern the original real assets and products; the fictional profile has no issuer, contracts, reserves, listings, partners or adoption.

evidence.statement: Circle describes Circle Mint as institutional access to mint and redeem its USDC and EURC, with customer and regional eligibility requirements.
evidence.subject: public_market
evidence.scope: Public Circle product description for its own assets. It does not offer or endorse the demo token.
evidence.independentCheck: Primary product page opened; no account access, conversion, redemption or fees tested.

evidence.statement: Stripe documentation lists USDC, USDP and USDG with token/network and merchant-location restrictions, fiat settlement and stablecoin refunds.
evidence.subject: public_market
evidence.scope: Verified documentation contents, not a completed merchant payment. Listing specific tokens does not imply support for arbitrary tokens.
evidence.independentCheck: Documentation opened; no merchant account, eligibility or payment flow tested.

evidence.statement: PayPal describes PYUSD payment and transfer uses for eligible accounts; the same page distinguishes available services from planned market expansion.
evidence.subject: public_market
evidence.scope: Real PYUSD product context only. Announcement and product copy are not independent adoption evidence.
evidence.independentCheck: Primary page opened. No account, reward rate, reserve state or geographic availability independently checked.

evidence.statement: Visa describes VSP as access to Open USD with limited availability, beta restrictions and API access coming soon.
evidence.subject: public_market
evidence.scope: Public product description and restrictions. This does not establish general third-party token eligibility.
evidence.independentCheck: Primary page opened; no Visa account, beta access or API integration tested.

evidence.statement: Mastercard announced work with Nuvei, Circle and Paxos on merchant stablecoin settlement in April 2025.
evidence.subject: public_market
evidence.scope: Existing named market initiative, not a new lead or evidence of support for a different issuer. Consumer tender and merchant settlement are separate legs.
evidence.independentCheck: Dated primary release opened; current production scope, transaction counts and commercial terms unverified.

evidence.statement: Paxos identifies itself as the issuer of PayPal USD and describes PYUSD access and redemption routes.
evidence.subject: public_market
evidence.scope: Real issuer/product relationship, retained under original names. No association with the demo profile.
evidence.independentCheck: Primary issuer page opened; redemption, reserve reports and contractual eligibility not independently reviewed.

evidence.statement: Coinbase publishes a USDC product page describing its dollar peg, intended redemption and region-dependent features.
evidence.subject: public_market
evidence.scope: UK-localized USDC context. Inconsistent network counts were not used; this is not a listing of the demo token.
evidence.independentCheck: Primary page opened; no executable quotes, balances, account eligibility or redemption tested.

evidence.statement: Solana Pay documentation defines an open payment protocol and reference implementations for developers.
evidence.subject: public_market
evidence.scope: Verified documentation contents. Protocol use is separate from a Solana Foundation partnership and current merchant adoption.
evidence.independentCheck: Protocol documentation opened; no app integration, blockchain state, token deployment or payment tested.

evidence.statement: Uniswap documentation explains that concentrated liquidity is allocated within price ranges and becomes inactive outside those ranges.
evidence.subject: public_market
evidence.scope: Protocol mechanics only. Total pool value is not the same as active executable depth; protocol access is not a Labs commercial deal.
evidence.independentCheck: Official documentation opened; no pool, quote, LP concentration or contract state queried.

evidence.statement: Visa announced USDC settlement pilots with merchant acquirers Worldpay and Nuvei in September 2023.
evidence.subject: public_market
evidence.scope: Historical named pilot. It does not prove current availability, support for another token or a new opportunity today.
evidence.independentCheck: Dated Visa release opened; no independent current Worldpay rollout or eligible product flow checked.

evidence.statement: Synthetic example: a future issuer might first test a narrow merchant acceptance need before proposing distribution.
evidence.subject: fictional_profile
evidence.scope: Illustrative hypothesis for the fictional profile. Sources supply market context, not evidence of a product, customer, relationship or demand.
evidence.independentCheck: Constructed demo example; no real issuer, buyer demand or partnership exists in this dataset.

evidence.statement: Synthetic example: a future issuer might compare existing issuer and settlement models before designing an interoperability proposal.
evidence.subject: fictional_profile
evidence.scope: Illustrative design question. Named companies retain their own products and existing public relationships; no shared demo-token initiative is implied.
evidence.independentCheck: Constructed demo example; token eligibility, legal route and economics are unspecified.

evidence.statement: Synthetic example: a future issuer should define conversion and exit requirements before comparing liquidity or adding a network.
evidence.subject: fictional_profile
evidence.scope: Illustrative research sequence. No demo token, pools, quotes, reserves or redemption route exist.
evidence.independentCheck: Constructed demo example; no balances, trades, authenticated quotes or chain state collected.

organizations.name: Stripe
organizations.relationshipSummary: No issuer relationship exists in this demo. The profile is fictional; public sources do not establish STABLE acceptance, listing or partnership.
organizations.publicContext: Documentation names accepted assets and eligibility restrictions; these concern real supported products.
organizations.relevance: Synthetic fit question: Could a narrowly defined merchant use case justify seeking a new acceptance route?
organizations.uncertainty: No demo token exists. New-token policy, merchant demand, product eligibility and commercial terms are unassessed.
nextQuestions: What would a real issuer need to satisfy the published token and merchant-location policy?
Which buyer problem remains after using already supported assets?

priorities.title: Define one merchant acceptance problem
priorities.thesis: Demo hypothesis: define one merchant settlement problem before considering a distribution route for a future issuer.
priorities.whyNow: Existing public products show how token and merchant eligibility constrain acceptance. This is an illustrative research sequence, not a launch signal.
priorities.nextAction: Write a hypothetical buyer/problem statement, required currency and jurisdiction. Compare it with existing supported assets; leave demand unproven.
assumptions: A real, eligible issuer and target buyer would be specified before a commercial recommendation.
A distinct merchant need would remain after comparing existing products.
disproves: No specific buyer or unmet settlement need can be identified.
Published token or regional policy excludes the proposed route, or existing products already solve the need.
priorities.confidenceReason: Public market context is documented. Fit for the fictional profile is synthetic; no acceptance, partnership, demand or commercial readiness is evidenced.

priorities.title: Map issuer and settlement constraints
priorities.thesis: Demo hypothesis: map redemption, custody and supported-token rules before suggesting an issuer or settlement partnership.
priorities.whyNow: Real issuer and network products provide design context, including beta restrictions and named existing partnerships. None establishes a relationship with the demo.
priorities.nextAction: Draft a hypothetical responsibilities matrix covering issuance, reserve evidence, eligibility, redemption, settlement and exceptions; mark every unspecified input unknown.
assumptions: A real profile would have a supportable issuance and redemption model.
A provider would permit the intended token and use case under documented conditions.
disproves: Responsibilities or eligibility cannot be established from credible evidence.
The proposed model adds no benefit or the route is closed to additional assets.
priorities.confidenceReason: Public market context is documented. Fit for the fictional profile is synthetic; no acceptance, partnership, demand or commercial readiness is evidenced.

priorities.title: Specify liquidity and exit requirements
priorities.thesis: Demo hypothesis: define size, execution cost and exit requirements before recommending a listing, pool or extra chain.
priorities.whyNow: Public exchange and protocol documentation describes useful comparison dimensions. There are no demo-token quotes, pools or transfer routes to evaluate.
priorities.nextAction: Create an empty benchmark template for size, bid/ask or price impact, all fees, timestamp, chain/asset identity and redemption path. Do not fill it with invented quotes.
assumptions: A real asset and authentic contracts would be identified before measurement.
A user conversion or redemption bottleneck would be evidenced.
disproves: There is no observable conversion or exit problem.
Existing routes meet the need, or improvements require uneconomic subsidies.
priorities.confidenceReason: Public market context is documented. Fit for the fictional profile is synthetic; no acceptance, partnership, demand or commercial readiness is evidenced.
